title: Make tfs_true_false the default for booleans
description:
Instead of adding a TFS(&tfs_true_false) to every boolean
field, make it the default if "strings" is NULL.

This seems to match the already existing documentation:

    If the Boolean field is to be displayed as "False" or "True", the
    'strings' field would be set to NULL.

notes.body:
added 11 commits
  • d0de08a7...fad2c1e3 - 9 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 78547a14 - Make tfs_true_false the default for booleans
  • 0ba19bd6 - Remove tfs_true_false
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/12208/diffs?diff_id=796682115&start_sha=d0de08a712a8b98e87346f1e19178703c1e33189)

This ended up causing #20262, because `dfilter_fvalue_from_string` checks `fvalue_from_string` *before* checking the value string (true_false_string), so for the oddball FT_BOOLEAN which has a true_false_string which maps 0 to "True" and 1 to "False", the "default" string is matched first.

I don't see a particular reason why this TFS string should be {"True", "False"} and not {"Null", "Not Null"} for example. The first is weird, the second is not weird and still semantically correct.

But after a superficial analysis I agree `flexray.nfi == "True"` should match the semantics of the oddball boolean. I would consider that a bug. I don't think the same is true for `flexray.nfi == True`. But I did not look very deeply into it, like I said.

> But after a superficial analysis I agree flexray.nfi == "True" should match the semantics of the oddball boolean. I would consider that a bug. I don't think the same is true for flexray.nfi == True

Yes, I agree on all points in my initial take as well. `True` and `"True"` are different here.

Unfortunately working around this is slightly annoying because of how `FT_PROTOCOL` and `FT_FRAMENUM` fields overload `strings` to mean something else (and `FT_PROTOCOL` *does* match string literals.)

There's some other annoying edge cases related to having multiple `FT_BOOLEAN` fields registered to the same abbreviation but with different `true_false_string`s.

If one of the fields has a null `true_false_string` but the other has a value like `tfs_set_notset`, should both match `field.abbrev == "True"` when the value is 1? Only the former matched before this change, but now it depends on which one was registered last.

I am now tempted to simply disallow having "True" or "False" in `true_false_strings`, particularly the reversed version.

Perhaps !11901 should be partially reverted and `mk_fvalue_from_val_string` should return to storing the default true_false_string there.

The problem that !11901 correctly identified was replacing the node with a FT_UINT64 fvalue instead of a FT_BOOLEAN, which !12189 fixed when bringing back the value string parsing for FT_BOOLEANs for non default values.
I'm not a huge fan of registering multiple fields to the same abbreviation and think that was a mistake. But either or both seems fine to me.

Multiple fields with the same abbreviation certainly creates some issues that are not correctly handled currently. The worst cases are all the fields that asn2wrs.py creates with non-compatible types (because the abbreviation only includes the last field name in the sequence and there's no clear way to rename it.)

The non-compatible case is at least considered to be a bug that should be fixed.

Even for type compatible fields with different abbrevs IMO it is a hack created so you don't have to type a sligthly longer OR expression, which could be done with a macro, or by creating a new field, or [pick one of N better solutions].

commits_data.message:
Make tfs_true_false the default for booleans

Instead of adding a TFS(&tfs_true_false) to every boolean
field, make it the default if "strings" is NULL.

This seems to match the already existing documentation:

    If the Boolean field is to be displayed as "False" or "True", the
    'strings' field would be set to NULL.
